title: Bram Stoker, Dracula recast
author: Salon
note: This whole-book remake includes vampiric violence, staking, and death. Period-true to Stoker, written without gore spectacle. Warn the room before you Host it; offer a midpoint pause if needed.

breaths.text: Can Hakan steamed up the Bosphorus toward a yalı that needed papers more than guests.
Istanbul split continents like a sentence with two subjects under crane-and-minaret sky.
Count Drago Mircea kept nocturnal hours and cold hands.
Can wrote Mine Yılmaz letters describing beauty and unease.
Light moved across water, glass, or stone like a slow argument no one would win cleanly.
Someone laughed in another room; laughter traveled like rumor with good shoes.
Breaths were counted as if they were coins on a thin table.
The glamorous surface held while private floorboards complained in the old language of cost.
A bell—church, tram, ferry, temple—rang for reasons that were not theirs alone.
Memory arrived without knocking and sat in the best chair with wet feet.
Duty cleared its throat in the dialect of families who confuse continuity with virtue.
Desire refused to take its coat and leave, even when the party had ended.
Outside, the city’s beauty continued shift work without consulting the wounded.
Nothing was simple except the weather’s indifference and the schedule’s cruelty.
They spoke carefully, which is how people bruise one another politely.
Night arranged its usual expensive dark over wards that photographed well.
Morning would demand faces; night allowed the true inventory of hungers.
Somewhere a boat, tram, train, or vaporetto kept schedule for the unbroken.
The plot, older than their recast names, waited with professional patience.
